summary: The bad entry point reads a line from a socket and embeds it directly into an HTTP error message via response.sendError(), reflecting attacker-controlled data into the HTML error page (CWE-81 reflected XSS). The fix HTML-encodes the data before it is placed into the error message, neutralizing markup/script while preserving the feature of reporting the received value. Only the sink in 22a is changed; the socket-reading source behavior is unchanged so valid inputs still flow through and are reported.

edits.old:
response.sendError(404, "
bad() - Parameter name has value " + data);
edits.new:
String encodedData = data.replace("&", "&").replace("<", "<").replace(">", ">").replace("\"", """).replace("'", "'"); response.sendError(404, "
bad() - Parameter name has value " + encodedData);
